chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Aqeeqa for the boy and the girl is the same.

key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةُ: Aqeeqa: The ritual sacrifice offered on the occasion of a child's birth

ai.seo_question: Is the Aqeeqa sacrifice different for boys and girls in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the Aqeeqa sacrifice is not gender-specific, a ruling that counters pre-Islamic customs which often favored males. By establishing equality between sons and daughters in this act of gratitude, it underscores the Shia emphasis on balanced familial rites and the spiritual value of both genders in Islamic tradition.
